---
title: "Figures on both sides"
description: "One figure floats to the right and a later one to the left."
format:
  html: default
  pdf: default
  typst:
    output-file: both-sides-typst.pdf
  docx: default
---

Each figure on this page picks its side with its own class:

```markdown
![Mean ratings by condition.](ratings.png){#fig-right .wrap-right width="35%"}

...

![Scores by hours of practice.](groups.png){#fig-left .wrap-left width="35%"}
```

## Result

![Mean ratings by condition.](../images/ratings.png){#fig-right .wrap-right width="35%"}

@fig-right has the class `.wrap-right`, so it sits on the right, and these
paragraphs flow on its left.

The figure wraps the paragraphs after it until a block that is not a
paragraph. Here that block is the horizontal rule below.

The rule starts below the figure, so the next figure starts on a clear
line.

* * *

![Scores by hours of practice.](../images/groups.png){#fig-left .wrap-left width="35%"}

@fig-left has the class `.wrap-left`, so it sits on the left, and these
paragraphs flow on its right.

Two wrapped figures right after each other do not both wrap: the first
keeps its normal layout. Put at least one paragraph after each figure, as
this page does.

The heading after this paragraph stops the second wrap.

## Next

A heading is not a paragraph, so wrapping stops before it.
